newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BK Vision to appeal ruling on UBS.
newsitem.headline: BK Vision to appeal ruling on UBS.

text.p: Investment fund BK Vision, chaired by maverick financier Martin Ebner, said it planned to appeal a recent ruling by a Zurich court that upheld Union Bank of Switzerland's (UBS) plans for a single share.
"BK Vision will in the coming days file a plea of nullity to a Zurich court as well as an appeal to the Supreme court," BK Vision president Martin Ebner told a news conference.

"We regret the decision, but it was to be expected," said a UBS spokeswoman in response to inquiries, noting that lawyer Peter Hafter already had announced an appeal and suits by BK Vision and Hafter were running parallel.
In early September Zurich's Commercial court upheld the legality of a decision by UBS shareholders in November 1994 to launch a single share.
Ebner gave a very critical view of this decision.
Following the decision by UBS shareholders, BK Vision and Hafter filed suits alleging wrongdoing, preventing the decision from taking effect.
Ebner, however, held out the possibility of dropping the appeal under appropriate conditions that gave shareholders greater say in UBS' strategic policy.
He further stated that BK Vision, UBS's single largest shareholder, still holds between eight and nine percent of UBS share capital.
Ebner again criticised UBS for being slow to take steps to maximise shareholder value, citing recent restructuring moves announced by the other two big Swiss banks.
"The restructuring announced by CS Holding and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) go in the direction that BK Vision already four years ago cited as a suitable basis for discussions with UBS," Ebner said.

Ebner and UBS have been locked in a long-standing battle over corporate governance for years, but the argument heated up in 1994 with UBS' decision to change its share struture, effectively dramatically reducing the voting power of BK Vision.
At that time it became clear that the legal wrangling would ultimately be decided by Switzerland's Supreme Court.

In addition to the two suits calling for annulment of the single share decision, BK Vision has filed suit, alleging criminal charges against UBS management and a civil suit against the board of directors.
These latter suits, however, do not affect the decision to introduce the single share.
